Thanks for the time earlier — quick recap and next steps from our discovery call.

Key points I captured:
- FinTechCo will require an on-demand Right-to-Be-Forgotten (RTBF) / delete API for end-user PII.
- Primary scope: chat transcripts, generated content, user profile metadata (PII fields), and embeddings.
- Data residency: production data must remain in US regions; backup copies currently stored in S3 buckets with multi-region replication — need confirmation of which regions.
- Retention / purge expectations: customers expect deletion from the live index within 24 hours of request; backups should be purged within 30 days where possible, longer if regulatory holds apply.
- Auditability: you need an attestation/audit log showing deletion events (timestamps, request IDs, retained artifacts).

Action items I promised to follow up on:
1) Outline our proposed RTBF workflow (live deletion + backup purge timeline + audit artifacts).
2) Clarify technical constraints around backups/snapshots and whether we can support immediate immutable snapshot deletion or only lifecycle-based purge.
3) Provide a sample addendum language for the contract outlining delete SLAs and exceptions for legal/regulatory holds.

Attached: redwood-rtbf-summary.pdf (high-level workflow we discussed).

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical follow-up with your security/ops folks to align on backup architecture and acceptable purge windows. I can make time tomorrow between 10–2 PT if that works.

Thanks,

Thanks Camila — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Deletion scope: yes to chat transcripts and profile PII. Embeddings can be scoped by user ID — we need an approach to map embeddings back to a user for purge.
- Backups: our compliance team requires backups to be purged within 30 days of an RTBF request where feasible. However, we also have rare regulatory holds (court orders, audits) that can extend retention; we’ll flag those cases.
- Snapshots: some of our infra snapshots are immutable for short windows (7–14 days) and then get pruned via lifecycle rules. We expect any vendor to either (a) schedule snapshot deletion on your side, or (b) accept the documented purge offset.
- Proof: we will need an exportable audit (CSV or signed attestation) showing deletion events, including request id, timestamp, affected object IDs, and the actor who performed the deletion.

I attached a spreadsheet with our initial questions: fintechco-rtbf-questions.xlsx.

James — can you confirm the list of acceptable proof formats and any constraints we should know before the follow-up call?

Best,
Susan Park
Data Privacy Lead, FinTechCo

Appreciate the detail, Susan — see below a proposed RTBF workflow and the implications we should align on. Attaching a PDF with the same flow: proposed-rtbf-workflow.pdf.

Proposed RTBF workflow (high level):
1) Request intake: customer triggers deletion via API or support portal; request gets a unique request_id.
2) Live deletion (T0–24h): remove PII and any user-linked data from active indices, application caches, and any hot KV stores within 24 hours. We replace with tombstones where necessary to maintain referential integrity.
3) Background purge (T+0–T+30 days): background jobs will remove data from cold storage and S3-based backups according to lifecycle rules. Because many backups are immutable snapshots, we surface an expected purge window (e.g., 30–60 days) and perform an expedited deletion where we control the underlying storage.
4) Audit & attestation: we will emit a signed deletion report (CSV + hash) listing request_id, timestamp, object keys removed, and operator ID. We can store the attestation in your portal and provide it as a downloadable link.

Technical constraints & notes:
- If FinTechCo’s infra uses third-party immutable snapshots outside our control, we will need your ops team to either (a) schedule snapshot deletion on your side, or (b) accept the documented purge offset.
- For embeddings: we can tag embeddings at write-time with a user_id so they can be queried and purged. If embeddings are deduplicated/clustered, purge might be best-effort depending on isolation.
- Audit logs: we can provide tamper-evident logs (WORM-like export) but cannot remove immutable system-level backups created by other infra providers.

Next steps I propose: technical sync with James and your infra team, and a follow-up legal/contract conversation to add the RTBF addendum we discussed. I’ll draft the addendum language after the technical sync.

Availability: I can do Mon 3/15 10–11 PT or Tue 3/16 1–3 PT. Which works best?

From: James Lee <james@fintechco.com>

Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: RTBF / delete request follow-up (FinTechCo)

Thanks Camila — that workflow helps. A couple of security/ops questions before we lock the addendum: 

1) KMS & key rotation: when you perform a purge, do you also rotate or retire keys associated with the deleted tenant so data encrypted at rest cannot be recovered from old snapshots?
2) Snapshots & immutability: can you enumerate which types of backups Redwood controls vs ones that are controlled by our infra? If Redwood controls a backup, can you perform an immediate object-level delete?
3) Logging & proof: the format you propose (CSV + hash) is fine. We also need the deletion events to be ingestible into our SIEM (JSON over S3 or a Syslog endpoint) so that our audit pipeline can validate.
4) Redaction vs deletion: for certain regulatory workflows we prefer redaction (masking PII) over full deletion for forensic reasons. Do you support redaction-only workflows and can you provide documented differences in guarantees (e.g., residual artifacts, index remnants)?

Also — please confirm the maximum SLA you can commit to for backup purge where Redwood fully controls the storage. We need concrete numbers for the contract.

On a separate note, can your attestation include a signed operator identity and be timestamped with an RFC3339 time? That would simplify our audit process.

Thanks,
James Lee
Security Engineering, FinTechCo
